notes: BUB1B compound-het candidate: c.2210T>G (p.Leu737Ter, stop_gained, ClinVar Pathogenic/Likely pathogenic VCV000533901.9, 2-star, MVA1-specific) + c.3006T>G (p.Asn1002Lys, missense, gnomAD singleton AC=1/1,461,878, falls within the kinase domain per UniProt O60566). Both heterozygous. Phase (cis/trans) not directly resolvable from proband-only short-read WGS: variants are ~11kb apart, beyond short-read fragment span, and GATK/Sentieon local phasing (PGT/PID) found no informative reads connecting them. Presumed compound heterozygous based on: (1) known pathogenic LOF + extremely rare kinase-domain missense co-occurring in the same well-established recessive disease gene, (2) full phenotype match (rhabdomyosarcoma, short stature, failure to thrive, IUGR) to the BUB1B-MVA spectrum, (3) extremely low prior probability of two independent rare BUB1B hits by chance. All frequency/clinical claims independently verified directly against gnomAD, ClinVar, and UniProt APIs (not just the VEP annotation proxy). See methods report for full ACMG evidence and explicit discussion of this phasing limitation.

BUB1B deep intronic variant c.2679-1026A>G, absent from gnomAD, sits physically between the two primary candidates. Not flagged as splice-altering by VEP's basic consequence call; SpliceAI query attempted but the service was unreachable (external outage), so cryptic-splice impact remains formally unassessed. Flagged for completeness, not scored as primary.
